headline: FIA President Confirms Qatar And Abu Dhabi Grand Prix Will Proceed
seoTitle: FIA Confirms Qatar and Abu Dhabi GP Will Proceed
metaDescription: FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem announced that the upcoming Formula 1 races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will take place as scheduled despite regional tensions.
aiSummaryBullets: The Federation Internationale de l'Automobile confirmed that the final two Formula 1 races of the season will proceed.
President Mohammed Ben Sulayem stated the events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi remain on schedule.
Earlier in the season, the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix was cancelled following the outbreak of conflict involving Iran, the United States, and Israel.
aiContextParagraph: The Federation Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) has clarified the status of the remaining 2026 Formula 1 season calendar following concerns regarding regional instability. According to FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem, the final two races of the season, hosted in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, are set to occur as originally planned. This announcement comes amid heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The status of the motorsport calendar has been a subject of scrutiny since the earlier cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix. That specific event was removed from the 2026 schedule following the commencement of military conflict between Iran and the combined forces of the United States and Israel. The FIA continues to monitor the regional situation while confirming that current plans for the final races in the United Arab Emirates and Qatar remain unchanged.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained traction through reports by international outlets confirming the continuity of the major sporting calendar amid regional geopolitical instability.
